content: We have thousands of human-written stories, discussions, interviews and reviews from today through the past 20+ years. Find them here: May 24, 2026, 2:01 PM · These days my mind is on music education, and how much we need it. Almost no child gets educated without music - even if they never receive a formal "music education." After all, how did you learn the very building blocks of your language - the alphabet? Was there a song? For the last couple of years I've been very involved in the American String Teachers Association, as President of the Los Angeles section in California. I've been thinking a lot about how to support music teachers, to get people working together, to encourage people to build orchestra programs. Making music together is the kind of activity that can allow kids to put their phones and tablets away and use their brains and bodies in the real world. It is cooperative, engaging, expressive - why have we cast this to the side, in education? And it all starts with someone who knows music, deciding to share that knowledge - to teach music. Which brings me to my question: Have you ever taught music? And there are so many ways you can be a teacher - maybe you actually teach in a classroom, or teach as a studio teacher. But maybe you have helped a child learn music by taking an active role in their lessons and practice - the "home teacher" for a child taking lessons. Please participate in the vote, and if you can say "yes" to more than one answer, then please pick whichever answer you most identify with. Then please share with us your thoughts on teaching and music education. May 24, 2026 at 07:46 PM · I voted studio teacher, but also have done classroom and currently am involved in church music classes and parenting musicians too :) (Last night we had the piano, recorder, and guitar all going on at the same time--each on a different song-chaos that makes me happy :) )  It's such a rewarding thing! May 24, 2026 at 08:48 PM · I voted yes, in some other way. I taught English language and literature in an international high school and participated in a lot of extra-curricular music activities. I would offer to cover music classes for absent music teachers to avoid being assigned covers in subjects of which I was ignorant and or untalented. May 24, 2026 at 09:00 PM · I have taught in my "studio" on and off since I was about 17. May 24, 2026 at 09:46 PM · I voted "Yes, in some other way," although I'm not a teacher - never taught in a class or studio setting; I never felt that was my calling. First instance: One afternoon, during my degree program, I coached a fellow-pupil in studio, with the watchful guidance of our professor. At one point, I told the pupil, "The D is too low." He fixed the pitch problem fast. Side note: His first language was Korean. Our professor's first language was Hungarian. Fortunately, we all had English in common, so instant communication was no problem. Second instance, while spending a weekend with my sister and her family: My second nephew had recently turned 11 y/o and was now big enough to handle a 4/4-size fiddle. It was around this time that I handed down my first 4/4-size instrument to him. I don't remember what the two of us played, but it was a fun time. I passed along to him a few pointers I had picked up from my own teachers. BTW, my nephew, at 11, handled a 4/4-size earlier than I had done. My first basic playing was on a 1/2-size in elementary school. Would you believe I didn't move up from 3/4 to 4/4 till I was 14 y/o? May 25, 2026 at 12:14 AM · Like a lot of musicians, I pieced together a career combining performing with conducting and teaching, both private lessons and classroom instruction. I've always learned from teaching, and I was particularly attracted to teaching "Music History and Appreciation" at a Prep School. I took the challenge of turning kids on to music as a personal mantra. My most vivid memory was a class where I played the orchestral themes to Batman, Spiderman, and Superman in class without identifying them. Once they figured out what the music was from, I asked them why they all had chosen music in a Classical style with a symphony orchestra. After some discussion, a rock guitar player in the class answered, "Because it's more emotional." A small victory, but I took it and still remember it! May 25, 2026 at 02:27 AM · After reading all of The Six Replies here from those who obviously Love the Violin and Love Music in differing genre's, I found this an interesting Group Response from all here willing to offer Help to all others obviously needing some additional 'tips' on violin playing and for Family Members plus other Groups who required encouragement and it is this which has me offering Gratitude to All on here Repliers due to a kindness in wanting to Help Others & not musicians yet some quite curious about How one Makes and Plays Music Alone & with many others either in a String Quartet or a School Orchestra, aka, in elementary school or Jr or Sr. High School Orchestra Settings or just for the fun & sake of learning How to play a violin or cello or other string cousins for the love and enjoyment of this activity requiring concentration and some love for beauty found in many glorious times prior of earlier compositions in many other centuries!! I hesitate to offer How I Voted due to vast self- experience teaching the violin since aged 8 taught by my String Educator father, known and more known as his String Teaching Methods became more US etc renowned across the United States and throughout Europe in due course with his USC Professorship Teaching USC Grads in Music How To Teach Strings if a Brass or Wind or Percussion musician!! My own musical background was and remains most rare for which I pinch myself almost every day and when one is asked for Advice from other Teachers or loving Musicians wishing to teach which a veteran Violin Soloist and Concertmaster when not On Tour as a soloist concert artist, I was early on taught 'How to Play in an Orchestra' by Poppa Ralph Matesky who wanted to ensure his daughter could not only survive in musical situations which could dissolve and leave one if Pro in a Pro Orchestra which had major financial funding issues to survive and do more than Survive but to return to one's Solo Violin Playing and also How To Teach one's in same school peers even if playing better which was very humbling to learn How to teach those struggling and forced to Figure Out How to do it and Do So with patience amid caring Not Judgement of those having issues or trouble in learning all sorts of technical 'Must Know's' to play & play seamlessly in concert with many others playing same music, aka, in an Orchestra where Blending In was always Imperative and if not able one might be asked to move to the back of one's section or even if not able to improve to Leave the Orchestra Class or Project some School Orchestras then preparing to go to Competitions within Cities lived or to Music compete State Wide with other Jr- Sr High Schools to win the Medals of Good Fine Superior so sought after in Jr & Sr High School!! All Paths to "Learning How to Teach" were covered and thoroughly by my String Education Father who helped several Generations to not only Learn How to Play in an Orchestra or Band but any Ensemble which required good solid musicianship and valid professional attitude even if not in a Pro loaded Orchestra or Marching Band, aka, the USC Marching Band for every USC Football Game vs many other Major University Marching Bands with all sort of competing with many others to play in a USC Final Game or even in The Super Bowl Game if being held then Locally in the LA Area!! My own Path led me after early on teaching by a Grand Mentor and Superb Violinist, Top of Class at Juilliard, Poppa Ralph and a Mom who accompanied fabled artists Toscha Seidel, Great Russian Violinist and prior in Mother Russia, Class-mate in Violin Great Teacher, Leopold Auer's Fabled Genius Violinist Class at the St. Petersburg Conservatory of Music Pupil's including Heifetz, Toscha Seidel, Sascha Lasserson, Efrem Zimbalist, Sr.; Kubelik; Mischa Elman; and Nathan Milstein, all of whom were Star Violinists and prior to fleeing then turned into 1917 Bolshevik Russia & overtaken by the Communists leaving less fortunate musicians little to live on or to earn a living from ... Life Lessons learned by All Above coming out of it all Most Well and Famously!! Having performed throughout all of Continental Europe; Scandinavia and Finland as Laureate of the First Sibelius International Violin Competition for the Centenery of Iconic Finnish Composer, Jean Sibelius' One Hundredth Birthday occurring then on 8th December 1965, I played at the Invitation of Madame Sibelius, then ailing at 92, yet wishing Yours Truly to Offer the Slow Movement or her late Grand Composer Husband's Violin Concerto which my Mentor, Jascha Heifetz, had forever championed during his Epic Concert Performing Career heralded throughout the World-always including the Sibelius Violin Concerto in his Concert Season Violin Concerti Repertoire with All Heifetz Fans having the luxury to Hear this Epic Violin Concerto from the Godly Hands of Heifetz with JH Heart and Soul very much inside this magnificent yet difficult work to play and Live!!! I learned it is Vitally important to communicate with many not knowing a Newer Work & in my Profession termed a Masterpiece prior to full public able to Hear and See Heifetz In Live Performance of a Mt. Everest Grand work for Violin with full Symphony Orchestra Concerto to be quite frankly Conquered and Beloved for a New Audience to Finnish moods & Messages conveyed by HEIFETZ which stayed in the Inner Hearing of so many first hearing "The Sibelius" loving it even humming it around the House!!! To teach One Must Have Done All to be Taught & more for Teaching what one can not do might be folly. Poppa Ralph in an Article for a major Music Publication in the US wrote this in his own words: "One Cannot Teach That which One Can Not Do!" How sobering a thought and "Truth is Beauty and Beauty Truth" by Keats who knew a thing or two!!! This is the Reason I begin my Reply complimenting all here who have thus far Replied for even if not able to play a violin concerto as the Sibelius or major Violin Concerti w/Orchestra many here have a Love for All Music and have already Offered help to their many needing it even if Not exactly saying so!!! This is Kind and Good for it has led to others never exposed to fine teaching wiser and more intrigued with the How's of Music Making and going forward in their own Lives to respect and love more music and Artists enabled to portray the Stories Of!!! Late on Sunday Evening of Memorial Day Weekend, I am at Peace after stopping by and reading the 6 Replies which give me Hope and Faith in a right now concerned for Passing On a Grand Legacy to those one fears will not wish to Learn???
